Expert Selection and Double-Blind Protocol
Auditor Qualification.
The evaluation panel comprises at least three (3) independent
domain auditors with expertise in local government service delivery and fluency in formal
English, Tagalog, and Bislish.
Audit Sample Allocation.
Auditors evaluate a preselected, category-balanced subset
of 20 final test scenario groups (4 per eBOSS category × 3 language variants = 60 distinct
query evaluations). To support the comparative baseline analysis, both Configuration A
(BM25 Baseline) and Configuration B (Proposed System) generate responses to all 60
queries, yielding a total of 120 system outputs. Each of the three domain auditors reviews
all 120 blinded and randomized responses, yielding a comprehensive evaluation dataset of
360 completed audit records.
Double-Blind Controls.
System identities are anonymized and masked. Answer pre-
sentation order is randomized across audit packages to eliminate order bias.
Scoring Rubric
Auditors evaluate responses independently using a 4-point ordinal rubric:

Statistical Verification of Inter-Rater Reliability
Following established departmental standards, inter-rater agreement among the
three expert auditors is statistically validated using Krippendorff’s alpha (α):
α = 1 − Do
De
(3.4)
where Do represents observed disagreement among raters and De represents disagreement
expected by chance.
An acceptance threshold of α ≥ 0.80 is established to confirm
statistically significant consensus across qualitative ratings.
3.3
Experimental Setup and Reproducibility
3.3.1
Hardware and Software Environment
All preprocessing, dense indexing, query normalization, retrieval scoring, local
model inference, and batch evaluations are conducted locally on a dedicated mobile work-
station to guarantee offline operational capability and reproducible latency benchmarks:
• Host Machine: Acer Predator Helios Neo 16 (PHN16-72-75Z0)
• Processor (CPU): 14th Generation Intel Core i7-14700HX (20 cores [8 Performance-
cores up to 5.40 GHz Turbo, 12 Efficient-cores up to 3.90 GHz], 28 threads, 33 MB
Intel Smart Cache)
• Graphics Processing Unit (GPU): NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU
(8 GB GDDR6 dedicated VRAM, Ada Lovelace architecture, 140 W Maximum
Graphics Power, CUDA Compute Capability 8.9)
• System Memory (RAM): 32 GB DDR5 dual-channel system memory running
at 5600 MHz
• Storage Infrastructure: 512 GB PCIe Gen4 NVMe M.2 Solid State Drive
• Operating System: Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS (Linux x86 64, 64-bit kernel 5.15.0)
under a dedicated development partition
• Programming Language & Execution Runtime: Python 3.10.12
• Inference Engine: Ollama v0.1.32 serving quantized open-weight Large Language
Models locally
• Key Software Libraries and Pinned Versions:
– torch==2.2.1+cu121 (CUDA-accelerated tensor backend)
– transformers==4.38.2 (Hugging Face tokenizer and pipeline execution)
– sentence-transformers==2.5.1 (Dense embedding generation)
– faiss-cpu==1.8.0 (Dense vector indexing and MIPS search)
– rank-bm25==0.2.2 (Probabilistic sparse retrieval index)
